//name: `freeboard` was taken in 2016 by an unrelated IOT dashboard (buglabs, still at
1.0.2), so the package is `freeboard-cli` and the BIN stays `freeboard`. npm's
getBinFromManifest uses the sole bin whatever it is called, so `npx freeboard-cli`
runs it and a global install puts `freeboard` on PATH, which is what the docs,
the landing page and the CLI's own examples all say.
name: freeboard-cli
description: Prove a DeFi position is solvent without revealing it — zero-knowledge solvency proofs on Midnight
author: SamY
//files: An ALLOWLIST, not an ignore list. npm previously fell back to .gitignore (it
warned) and shipped all 123 tracked files: .claude/settings.local.json with 326
permission entries naming absolute home paths and localhost ports, the whole
notes/ roadmap, the entire web/ app, both compose files. Meanwhile it EXCLUDED
contracts/managed/ — which .gitignore drops but the runtime requires, since
NodeZkConfigProvider reads the prover keys from there and cli.js dynamically
imports contract/index.js. So the published package was simultaneously too big
and missing the one thing it could not run without.
contracts/managed is ~844K, which is fine for npm.

scripts.devnet:stop-all: docker compose -f docker-compose.ledger9.yml down; docker compose -f docker-compose.yml down
scripts.//clean: Build artifacts only. State moved out of the repo into the per-user state home (see src/paths.ts), so a wildcard rm here would silently miss it — and a wildcard rm THERE would delete a wallet and an attester key, which is not something a script called `clean` should do without being asked. `clean:state` is the explicit one.
scripts.//prepack: The published package runs from dist/, so a publish without a build ships a stale or absent one. prepack runs on `npm pack` and `npm publish` (not on install), which makes that unreachable rather than merely documented.
scripts.//scripts-hook: Every entry point that reaches the Midnight SDK runs tsx with --import ./bin/register-fetch.mjs, which is the same cross-fetch redirect the published `freeboard` bin installs. `network` and `test:cache` are pure fs and do not need it.

//dependencies: WHY @midnight-ntwrk/wallet-sdk-utilities IS A DIRECT DEPENDENCY, not an override.
wallet-sdk declares 1.2.0, and 1.2.0 ships no Clock module — importing the SDK barrel
dies at module load. That was fixed with an `overrides` entry, which npm honours only
in a root project, so every consumer of this package got the broken resolution back.
Verified: a fresh install of wallet-sdk alone resolves 1.2.0 and throws "does not
provide an export named 'Clock'"; the direct dependency hoists 1.2.1 and the barrel
THIS NOTE LIVES AT THE TOP LEVEL, NOT INSIDE `dependencies`. It used to sit in there
as a `//`-prefixed key. npm reads EVERY key of `dependencies` as a package name, so
that turned the prose into a spec and any install of the published tarball died with
EINVALIDPACKAGENAME — invisible in this repo, because installing the project itself
never resolves it. Comment keys are safe at the top level and inside `scripts`; they
are not safe inside a dependency map.
//overrides: cross-fetch is gone from here. A `file:` override cannot survive publish, and the reason it existed is now handled inside the process: bin/freeboard.mjs registers a loader hook that resolves cross-fetch to bin/cross-fetch-shim.cjs, which delegates to Node's built-in fetch. See that file for the measurements.
